reason: This holds. catalog.py:1461-1472 sets mcp=True only for kind=='read_handler' (except backtest_summary), so every host_action (portfolio_add_position/update/delete, write_note, add/remove_from_watchlist, save_layout, save_screen, etc.) is never projected to the external MCP surface. That contradicts US5 acceptance 3 ('no capability reachable to one consumer but not the other'), the constitution rule that a capability must not exist for only one consumer, and the spec edge case at spec.md:789-790 ('External MCP client requests a mutating tool -> same gate ... same confirmation path'). One nuance: the omission is a deliberate rule written down in a catalog.py comment ('host actions are inherently local ... never projected'), not a silent accident, but the spec was never amended to match. propose_order is in the listed set but closes with the trading removal; the portfolio, notes and watchlist host actions stay in scope.
evidence_checked: Opened the catalog projection rule and mcp_capabilities(), mcp_server tool registration and _make_catalog_tool, agent_tools.invoke_tool, and the spec US5, FR-020..022 and edge-case text at HEAD. Listing MCP tools would need a streamable-HTTP POST to :52152, so I did not drive it; the code settles the claim.
repro_check: sed -n 1461,1472p catalog.py -> mcp=(cap.kind == 'read_handler' and cid not in _MCP_INTERNAL_ONLY), so no host_action ever reaches mcp_capabilities() and mcp_server only add_tool()s that list.

reason: This is the same defect as INT-spec-90-1 and gets the same correction; dedupe onto one register entry. The remaining leak covers only unclassified errors on single-symbol routes and the chart catch, so severity drops medium->low.
